rationale:
I judged the tests in `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/outline_content.rs` adequate for `requirements.sdk.outlines.items`. I did not request implementation source. The mandatory inputs were enough to map each obligation to a test.

**Whole-file outline, including for a selected item**
- `selected_contents_outlive_handles_and_later_file_edits` builds a selected content from both `from_id` and `select`. It asserts that `selected.outline().items.len()` is 3, the whole file's outline. It also checks that a root can still be selected from the selected value.
- `markdown_heading_levels_resolve_encoded_duplicates_and_anonymous_items` and `rust_items_attach_documentation_and_preserve_structural_hashes` assert `std::ptr::eq(second.outline(), contents.outline())`. That shows the selected value exposes the same retained outline.

**Root first, then items in source preorder; full selectors with ancestry**
- `rust_items_attach_documentation_and_preserve_structural_hashes` asserts the exact selector sequence `["", "mod[auth]", "mod[auth]/fn[check]", "mod[auth]/struct[Token]", "fn[last]"]`. It also asserts the kinds. A top-level item following a nested module checks preorder, and the root is first.
- The Markdown tests assert the ordered nested selectors, including the `#1` and `#2` duplicates and the anonymous `section@` and `block@` forms.
- The plain-text tests cover `line` items in source order.

**Struct shape**
- The tests read `items`, `selector`, `kind`, `span` and `structural_hash` directly.
- `unknown_extensions_keep_nonblank_lines_and_content_selectors` checks that the selector prefix equals `structural_hash[..12]`.
- `rust_items_attach_documentation_and_preserve_structural_hashes` checks that `selected.structural_hash()` equals `item.structural_hash` for every item.

**Spans**
- Byte offsets and unicode: `unicode_spans_use_bytes_and_whitespace_only_lines_create_no_items` uses `é` and `🦀` and asserts the exact byte ranges `[0..len, 0..2, 6..10]`. It also checks that slicing the source gives the expected text.
- Valid slicing: `bundled_languages_claim_extensions_and_supply_the_same_public_outline` checks `source.get(item.span)` for every item in all bundled languages. The Markdown tests do the same.
- Exclusive end: the Rust test asserts `source[..span.end].ends_with("fn check() { allow(); }")`, so the end is exclusive and exact. It also asserts that `source[span]` equals the selected text for every item.
- Attached source: the Rust test asserts that the span starts at `/// Check tokens.` and includes `#[inline]`. The setext tests (`multiline_setext_sections_keep_original_source_spans_and_skip_code` and `setext_sections_inside_directives_lists_and_quotes_retain_container_spans`) check Markdown's own span rules. Those rules cover the multi-line heading start, the container underline, and fenced code staying inside the section.
- Root selector and span: root selector `""` and span `0..source.len()` are asserted in the plain-text, Rust, Markdown, bundled-language and unicode tests. The empty-source case asserts `0..0`.

**Attached-source rules for other languages**
Rules for Python, TypeScript, CSS, TOML and YAML are language-specific. They belong to the per-language item requirements, not to this general requirement, so I did not treat them as gaps here. I found no other class of input that this requirement distinguishes and the tests miss.

No acknowledgments (`{fixme}`) apply.

text: :::{req} items
`OutlineContent::outline` exposes the outline of its whole retained file,
including when the content value selects one item. The outline lists the file
root first, followed by its items in source preorder. Full selectors identify
items and their ancestry under {cite}`requirements.references.outline_selectors`.
```rust,ignore
use std::ops::Range;
pub struct Outline {
pub items: Vec<OutlineItem>,
pub struct OutlineItem {
pub selector: String,
pub kind: String,
pub span: Range<usize>,
pub structural_hash: String,
impl OutlineContent {
pub fn outline(&self) -> &Outline;
Each span uses byte offsets into the supplied source snapshot, with an exclusive
end and boundaries valid for slicing that text. It includes the item's attached
source under the language's rules. The root has an empty selector and span
`0..source.len()`.
:::{req} outline_selectors
An outline selector MUST be a `/`-separated path of segments from the file's
root node to an outline node; the empty selector MUST select the root node. A
named node's segment MUST be `kind[name]`. An anonymous node's segment MUST be
`kind@hash`, where `hash` is the first twelve hexadecimal digits of its identity
hash under {cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash`. Siblings whose
segments would otherwise be identical MUST be disambiguated by `#N`, their
one-based position among those siblings in source order, except `line` nodes:
identical lines are interchangeable, so a `line` selector MUST resolve when any
line with that content exists in the file. In names, `%`, `[`, `]`, `/`, `#`,
`@`, and whitespace MUST be percent-encoded as UTF-8 bytes, so selectors are
reversible. Line numbers MUST NOT form part of a selector.
